info.title: TatvaCare Partner API
info.description:
The Partner API pushes leads into TatvaCare and reads their state back. The key determines which fields may be read and written, and which product line a lead belongs to. There is no fixed payload.

## What this API does

Leads are created or updated by phone (idempotent), one at a time or in bulk. They are read singly or listed, and deleted by id. The schema is discovered at runtime: `lead_schema` returns exactly what a key may send and read.

## The shape

A lead has top-level fields (such as `first_name`, `mobile_no`, `status`) and child tables sent as arrays (such as `custom_lab_profile` and `custom_plan_profile`). A lead is unique per phone within its product line and group. Re-sending the same phone updates that lead and never duplicates it, so every write is safe to retry. Product line and group are fixed to the key. The program is a mutable attribute (sent in List mode, stamped in Forced mode) and is never part of identity.

## Where to start

- [Overview](/partner-welcome) and [Quickstart](/partner-quickstart) introduce the API.
- [`lead_schema`](/discover-schema) is called first when building a request; it returns the available fields, which of them are required, and how child tables behave.
- [Reading responses](/reading-values) and [Errors](/partner-errors) cover reading a response.

Every endpoint has a live console below. A saved API key ([Authentication](/partner-validate-key)) is reused on every request.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
Every request needs an `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>
```

The literal lowercase `token`, a single space, then the key and secret joined by a colon.

A key saved via [Authentication](/partner-validate-key) is reused by the console on every request. The verification call below confirms the header before any lead call.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description:
The gated lead methods are the entire lead surface. Each one resolves what the key is permitted to do: the fixed product line, and the fields that may be sent and read. The raw resource route for `CRM Lead` is not available to partner keys (it returns `403`); these methods are the supported path.

| HTTP method | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `lead_schema` | Discovery: exactly the fields the key may send and read, plus the routing mode. |
| GET | `lead_get` | Read one lead by `name` or `mobile_no`. |
| POST | `lead_create` | Create or upsert by phone. Returns the CRM `name`. |
| PUT | `lead_update` | Update a lead by CRM `name` (the id `lead_create` returned). |
| DELETE | `lead_delete` | Delete a lead by CRM `name` (a lead with linked activity cannot be deleted). |
| POST | `lead_create_bulk` | `{"leads":[{...}]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |
| PUT | `lead_update_bulk` | `{"updates":[{"name":...}]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |
| DELETE | `lead_delete_bulk` | `{"names":[...]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |
| POST | `lead_get_bulk` | `{"names":[...]}` or `{"mobile_nos":[...]}` (up to 100). Out-of-scope ids are omitted. |
| GET | `lead_list` | Curated filters and pagination, always scoped to the line. |

**`lead_create` is the default write path.** It is idempotent on the lead identity, safe to retry, and performs the lookup-or-create.

### Lead identity and dedup

A lead is unique per phone, product line, and group ([Lead identity](/concepts)). Routing is never sent, because the line is fixed to the key, so dedup reduces to phone within the line: `lead_create` finds the lead matching the line and that phone and updates it, or creates a new one. The same phone on a different line is a separate lead.

### Child profile writes

Profile children (`custom_plan_profile`, `custom_lab_profile`) are sent as embedded arrays inside the body. Writes merge field by field into the existing row: fields that are sent are overlaid, fields that are omitted are left alone. A partial write never wipes the row. This holds for `lead_create`, `lead_update`, and their bulk forms.

### Routing

Routing (`source`, line, group, program) is forced from the key. Any routing field that is sent is ignored.

### Field validation

- Allowed fields are per key. `lead_schema` lists exactly what a key may send; anything outside that list is dropped. `mobile_no` is always allowed (the anchor).
- Required to create: `mobile_no`. `first_name` and `status` are default-filled when omitted.
- Some values are checked against an allowed set (for example `status`, `source`, and program). The valid values are returned by `lead_schema`.

### Reading leads

Three paths: `lead_get` (one, by `name` or `mobile_no`), `lead_get_bulk` (many), `lead_list` (filtered and paginated). All return only the key's allowed fields and only leads on the caller's line.

`lead_list` honours a curated set of filters only, never arbitrary fields:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `status` | exact lead status |
| `created_after` / `created_before` | creation date range |
| `updated_after` / `updated_before` | last-modified date range |
| `mobile_no` | exact phone |
| `limit` | page size (default 20, max 200) |
| `offset` | rows to skip (paging) |

List results return curated parent fields and no children; `lead_get` returns a full record. The response nests the page under `data`: `{"status":"success","action":"fetched","data":{"total":..,"count":..,"offset":..,"limit":..,"leads":[..]}}`.

### Bulk partial success

Every bulk method runs each record independently: one bad row reports its error, the rest still commit. The response is `{"status":"success","summary":{..},"results":[{"index":..,"status":"success"|"error",..}]}`.

### Reading children

`lead_get` and `lead_get_bulk` return the profile children inline, filtered to the key's allowed fields. Child tables cannot be read on their own; they are always read through the parent lead.

tags.name: Activities
tags.description:
Activities are logged on a lead. An activity is a task of a configured activity type, scoped to the lead's product line and group. The same key that writes leads writes activities: there is no per-entity enablement, and one key governs all four entity APIs.

| HTTP method | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `activity_schema` | Discovery by lead: the activity types available to a lead, each with its field schema. |
| GET | `activity_get` | Read one activity by task `name`. |
| POST | `activity_create` | Create or upsert (deduped on `external_id`). |
| PUT | `activity_update` | Re-apply values to an activity by `name`. |
| DELETE | `activity_delete` | Delete an activity by `name`. |
| POST | `activity_create_bulk` | `{"activities":[...]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |
| POST | `activity_get_bulk` | `{"names":[...]}` or `{"external_ids":[...]}` (up to 100). |
| GET | `activity_list` | By lead (plus optional `task_type` and `status`), paginated. |

### Discover before sending

Activity fields are scoped to the lead: different leads expose different types and fields. `activity_schema?lead=<id>` (or `?mobile_no=`) is called first, and values are sent and read keyed by the schema `fieldname` under `values`. A field list must not be hardcoded.

### Idempotency

`external_id` is the idempotency key: re-sending the same `external_id` updates that activity and never doubles it. Optional `created_at` backdates the activity for historical loads.

### Scope

Every activity resolves its lead through the shared scoped resolver: an out-of-scope or missing lead returns the same generic not-found. Bulk endpoints take up to 100 records per call, with per-row partial success. See [Rate limits](/rate-limits).

tags.name: Files
tags.description:
Files are attached to a lead (or to a scoped activity or note on that lead). The same key as leads, with no per-entity enablement.

| HTTP method | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `file_attach` | Decode or download the bytes and attach to a lead (or a scoped activity or note). |
| GET | `file_get` | Read one file's metadata and proxy url. |
| GET | `file_list` | A lead's files (optional `file_type`), paginated. |
| DELETE | `file_delete` | Delete a file by `name`. |
| POST | `file_attach_bulk` | `{"files":[...]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |

### Always private

Every file attached through this API is private. `is_private` is always `true` and `file_url` is a proxy url, never a raw storage key or local path. The bytes are sent either as a downloadable `file_url` (fetched by the server) or as `content_base64`. Exactly one is sent.

### Idempotency

`external_id` is the idempotency key: re-attaching the same `external_id` to the same record returns the existing file with `action: "exists"` and never duplicates it.

### Scope

The lead (or its activity or note) is scoped through the shared resolver: out-of-scope or missing is the same generic not-found. Bulk endpoints take up to 100 records per call, with per-row partial success. See [Rate limits](/rate-limits).

tags.name: Calls
tags.description:
Calls are logged on a lead. A call is stored in the same call log the telephony integration writes to. The same key as leads, with no per-entity enablement.

| HTTP method | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `call_create` | Create or upsert a call log (deduped on `external_id`). |
| GET | `call_get` | Read one call by `name`. |
| GET | `call_list` | A lead's calls (plus optional `direction` and `status`), paginated. |
| DELETE | `call_delete` | Delete a call by `name`. |
| POST | `call_create_bulk` | `{"calls":[...]}` (up to 100). Partial success. |

### Attribution: `lead` is always read

`lead` or `mobile_no` attaches the call explicitly (scoped to the line). Omitting both lets the server strict-match the customer number (`from_number` on Inbound, `to_number` on Outbound), scoped to the line. No match, or an ambiguous match, leaves the call unlinked and `lead` returns `null`, never on the wrong lead. `lead` is always read to confirm whether the call was linked.

### Idempotency

`external_id` is the idempotency key: re-sending the same `external_id` updates that call and never doubles it. The returned `name` is the call's own id, which is not the `external_id`. Optional `started_at` backdates the call on insert.

### Scope

Reads and deletes are scoped to the line, and an unlinked call is never visible to a partner. Bulk endpoints take up to 100 records per call, with per-row partial success. See [Rate limits](/rate-limits).

CRMLeadUniversal.description: Universal fields on the lead itself. The top-level fields a key may send and read live here, and child tables embed as arrays. The exact fields a key is granted are listed by `lead_schema`.

name.description: The lead's unique id, in the form `CRM-LEAD-YYYY-NNNNN`. Read-only: the server generates it, so never send it on a create.

first_name.description: First name. If it is unknown, `(no name)` is filled in when it is omitted on create.

mobile_no.description: Required. The dedup anchor, together with the product line and group. E.164 format: `+<country code><digits>`, no spaces or hyphens.

custom_alternate_number.description: Alternate contact phone (optional). E.164, same as `mobile_no`.

status.description: Required on create. The lead's lifecycle status. New leads start at `New`. Read the allowed values from `lead_schema`.

source.description: Lead acquisition channel. Read the allowed values from `lead_schema`.

lead_owner.description: Email of the CRM user who owns this lead. Set it only to an existing CRM user's email, otherwise leave it blank.

lost_reason.description: Required when `status` is `Junk` or `Unqualified`. Read the allowed values from `lead_schema`.

lost_notes.description: Free-text note explaining why the lead was lost.

custom_vertical.description: The product line. Fixed to the key and stamped server-side, so it is never sent by the caller.

custom_group.description: The group within the product line. Fixed to the key and stamped server-side, so it is never sent by the caller.

custom_current_program.description: The lead's current program. A mutable attribute, not part of identity. Whether it is sent depends on the key's program mode (see `lead_schema`).

custom_previous_program.description: The lead's previous program if it transitioned. Records the last switch only.

custom_origin_vertical.description: The product line the lead first entered through. Captured once and never updated.

custom_source_origin.description: Where the lead source data originated. Deprecated for new writes; use `source` instead.

custom_patient_id.description: External identifier from the source system.

custom_lsq_prospect_id.description: Legacy migration identifier. Not populated for new leads.

custom_lead_gen_id.description: External lead-generation identifier (campaign or form submission id).

custom_patient_age.description: Age in years. Caller-provided; not derived from the date of birth.

custom_caregiver_relation.description: Caregiver's relationship to the lead (for example Spouse, Daughter, Son).

custom_plan_profile.description: Plan, subscription, program, payment, and acquisition data, sent as an array. Writes merge field by field into the existing row, so a partial write never wipes it. Discover the exact fields via `lead_schema`.

custom_lab_profile.description: Lab values, vitals, conditions, and scores, sent as an array. Discover the exact fields via `lead_schema`.

custom_care_providers_profile.description: Care team: coaches, relationship manager, therapist, doctor, hospital, sent as an array. Discover the exact fields via `lead_schema`.

lead_name.description: Read-only. Auto-computed from `first_name` and `last_name`. Never write it.

creation.description: Read-only. When the lead was created.

modified.description: Read-only. When the lead was last modified. Useful for change tracking and delta sync.

PlanProfile.description: A plan, subscription, or program profile row, sent as a JSON array under `custom_plan_profile`. The exact fields available are key-specific and are discovered via `lead_schema` (`data.children.custom_plan_profile.fields`). A field list must not be hardcoded.

name.description: The row's unique id (read-only; present when a lead is read back).

LabProfile.description: A lab-values and vitals profile row, sent as a JSON array under `custom_lab_profile`. The exact fields available are key-specific and are discovered via `lead_schema` (`data.children.custom_lab_profile.fields`). A field list must not be hardcoded.

name.description: The row's unique id (read-only; present when a lead is read back).

CareProvidersProfile.description: A care-team and providers profile row, sent as a JSON array under `custom_care_providers_profile`. The exact fields available are key-specific and are discovered via `lead_schema` (`data.children.custom_care_providers_profile.fields`). A field list must not be hardcoded.

name.description: The row's unique id (read-only; present when a lead is read back).

UpsertLeadRequest.description: Request body for `lead_create`. Only `mobile_no` is strictly required (the dedup anchor); `first_name` and `status` are default-filled if missing (`(no name)` and `New`). All other fields are optional and must be within the fields the key is allowed to send (`lead_schema` lists them). Routing is never sent; it is set server-side. Profile children embed as arrays and merge field by field.

LeadUpdateRequest.description: Request body for `lead_update`. Carries the CRM `name` (the id `lead_create` returned) plus any allowed fields to change. Parent fields that are sent are updated, fields that are omitted are left alone, and profile children merge field by field. Routing cannot be changed; it is fixed to the key.

PartnerError.description: The single error envelope returned by every failure. Branch on `error.code`; the full `error.code`-to-HTTP map is on the [Errors](/partner-errors) page.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on the message text.

fields.description: Present on some `validation_error`s, the field name(s) that failed.

retry_after.description: Present only on `rate_limited` (429): seconds until the key's budget resets.

PartnerWriteResponse.description: Success envelope from `lead_create` / `lead_update` / `lead_delete`. **Top-level, there is no `message` wrapper** (the gated partner methods emit the body directly). Read `status` first, then `action`, then `data`. A failure instead returns the PartnerError envelope with a non-2xx status.

action.description: What happened: a new lead, an upsert onto an existing one, or a delete.

name.description: CRM Lead id (e.g. `CRM-LEAD-2026-00123`). PUT this back to `lead_update`.

source.description: Lead source, forced from the key for partners.

PartnerReadResponse.description: Success envelope from `lead_get` / `lead_list`. Top-level (no `message` wrapper). `action` is `fetched`; `data` carries the curated lead (`lead_get`) or the page object (`lead_list`).

data.description: The curated lead (`lead_get`) or the page object `{total,count,offset,limit,leads[]}` (`lead_list`).

PartnerSchemaResponse.description: Success envelope from `lead_schema`. Top-level (no `message` wrapper), no `action`. `data` holds the fields THIS key may send/read, the child-write rules, dedup grain, bulk limits, and routing mode.

children.description: Per child table: `{multi_row, key_field, fields[]}`. `multi_row:true` means upsert-by-key on `key_field`.

child_write.description: How to send child arrays + the upsert-by-key rule.

dedup.description: The lead identity (mobile_no + product line + group).

routing.description: `forced` / `list` / `none` for a partner (line + group always fixed); `caller-supplied` for a trusted internal caller.

PartnerBulkResultEntry.description: One record's outcome in a bulk response. `status` is `success` or `error` per row. On `success`: `action`+`name` (writes) or `data` (lead_get_bulk). On `error`: the same `error:{code,message}` block as the top-level PartnerError.

index.description: 0-based position in the request array (results are input-ordered).

action.description: Present on a successful write row.

name.description: CRM Lead id (present on a successful write row).

data.description: Curated lead (present on a successful `lead_get_bulk` row).

error.description: Present on a failed row (its savepoint rolled back).

PartnerBulkResponse.description: Partial-success envelope shared by every bulk method. Top-level (no `message` wrapper). Each record runs in its own savepoint, one bad row reports its error, the rest still commit. `summary` is `{total,succeeded,failed}` for writes and `{requested,found,not_found}` for `lead_get_bulk`. Inspect `results[].status` per row; the HTTP status is 200 even when some rows failed.

status.description: `success`, the batch ran (individual rows may have failed).

summary.description: Counts: a write returns `{total,succeeded,failed}`, and a get returns `{requested,found,not_found}`.

ActivitySchemaField.description: One field on an activity type, as returned by `activity_schema`. Send and read activity values keyed by `fieldname` (never hardcode a list, discover them per type).

fieldname.description: The key to send/read this value under inside the activity `values` object.

options.description: For `Link` the target doctype; for `Select` the newline-separated options; else null.

reqd.description: `1` means the field is required for this activity type.

ActivityType.description: One line-scoped activity type available to a lead, returned by `activity_schema`. Pick a `name` and send its `fields` under `values`.

name.description: The activity type id, send it as `task_type` on create/update.

is_logged_complete.description: `1` means logging this activity marks it complete (it carries no separate status workflow).

fields.description: The fields an integrator may send under `values` for this type.

Activity.description: The partner-facing shape of an activity. `values` is re-keyed to the type's schema `fieldname`s; read and write activity data through `values`, never internal fields.

name.description: The activity id, the activity's unique id (PUT/DELETE this back).

lead.description: The CRM Lead this activity hangs off.

external_id.description: **Idempotency key** (stored in `custom_lsq_activity_id`). Re-sending the same `external_id` updates that activity, never doubles.

values.description: The activity's data, keyed by the type's schema `fieldname`s (discover them via `activity_schema`).

ActivityUpsertRequest.description: Body for `activity_create` / `activity_update`. Target a lead by `lead` (CRM name) OR `mobile_no`. `task_type` names the activity type; `values` carries data keyed by the type's `fieldname`s (from `activity_schema`). `external_id` is the idempotency key, re-send to update, never doubles.

lead.description: CRM Lead id. Send this OR `mobile_no`.

external_id.description: Idempotency key (stored in `custom_lsq_activity_id`). Re-sending the same value updates that activity instead of creating a new one.

values.description: Activity data keyed by the type's schema `fieldname`s. Required fields per type come from `activity_schema`.

created_at.description: Optional. Backdates the activity's `creation` (historical / migration load). Ignored on update.

name.description: **`activity_update` only**, the activity id to update.

File.description: The partner-facing shape of a file on a lead (or a scoped activity task). Files are **always private**; `file_url` is a proxy URL, never a raw storage key or local path.

name.description: The File id, the file's unique id (DELETE this back).

file_type.description: The document category (stored in `custom_file_type`), e.g. `Lab Report`, `Prescription`, caller-supplied.

external_id.description: **Idempotency key** (stored in `custom_lsq_attachment_id`). Re-attaching the same `external_id` to the same record returns the existing file (`action: exists`).

file_url.description: Proxy URL to fetch the (private) bytes, never a raw storage key or local path.

is_private.description: Always `true`, files attached via this API are private by design.

attached_to_doctype.description: What the file hangs off, the lead, or a scoped activity task.

attached_to_name.description: The id of the lead or task the file is attached to.

FileAttachRequest.description: Body for `file_attach`. Target a lead by `lead` OR `mobile_no` (optionally a scoped `activity` task). Supply the bytes as a downloadable `file_url` OR `content_base64` (exactly one). Idempotent on `external_id` + the target record.

lead.description: CRM Lead id. Send this OR `mobile_no`.

activity.description: Optional activity id to attach the file to instead of the lead. The activity must belong to this lead (else generic not-found).

note.description: Optional note id to attach the file to instead of the lead. The note must belong to the same lead. Send `activity` or `note`, not both.

external_id.description: **Required.** Idempotency key (stored in `custom_lsq_attachment_id`). Re-attaching the same value to the same record returns the existing file (`action: exists`).

file_url.description: A (signed / expiring) URL the server downloads the bytes from. Send this OR `content_base64`.

content_base64.description: The file bytes, base64-encoded. Send this OR `file_url`.

Call.description: The partner-facing shape of a call log. **`lead` may be `null`** when no phone match or an ambiguous (2+) match was found; fail-closed attribution never attaches a call to the wrong lead. Always read `lead` to know whether the call was linked.

name.description: The CRM Call Log id (the autonamed row name; NOT the `external_id`).

external_id.description: **Idempotency key** (stored in `custom_external_id`). Re-sending the same value updates that call log, never doubles.

lead.description: The linked CRM Lead, **`null` when attribution found no/ambiguous match** (the call is left unlinked, never attached to a wrong lead). Read this.

direction.description: Call direction (maps to the call log `type`: Inbound to Incoming, Outbound to Outgoing).

recording_url.description: URL of the call recording, if any.

CallUpsertRequest.description: Body for `call_create`. `external_id` (idempotency key) and `direction` are required. Attribution: `lead` or `mobile_no` targets a lead explicitly (line-scoped); omitting both lets the server strict-match the customer number (`from_number` on Inbound, `to_number` on Outbound) within the caller's line. No match, or an ambiguous match, leaves the call unlinked (`lead: null`), never on a wrong lead.

external_id.description: **Required.** Idempotency key (stored in `custom_external_id`). Re-sending the same value updates that call log, never doubles.

lead.description: Optional CRM Lead id to attach to (line-scoped). If sent with `mobile_no`, `lead` wins.

mobile_no.description: Optional lead phone (auto-normalized) to attach to (line-scoped).

from_number.description: Calling party number. On an Inbound call with no `lead`/`mobile_no`, this is the customer number used for attribution.

to_number.description: Called party number. On an Outbound call with no `lead`/`mobile_no`, this is the customer number used for attribution.

status.description: Call status. Defaults to `Completed` on insert if omitted.

started_at.description: Call start time. On insert it also backdates the row's `creation` (historical load).

EntityListResponse.description: Success envelope from the entity list endpoints (`activity_list` / `file_list` / `call_list`). Top-level (no `message` wrapper), `action: fetched`. `data` is a page object with `total/count/offset/limit/has_more` plus the entity array (`activities` / `files` / `calls`).

total.description: Total rows matching the filter (across all pages).

data.description: Page object; the entity array is keyed `activities` / `files` / `calls` depending on the endpoint.

EntityReadResponse.description: Success envelope from the entity single-read / write endpoints (`*_get`, `activity_create/update`, `file_attach`, `call_create`, `activity_schema`). Top-level (no `message` wrapper). `action` reflects what happened; `data` is the entity (Activity / File / Call) or the schema/discovery object.

data.description: The entity (Activity / File / Call), the `{name}` on a delete, or the discovery object on `activity_schema`.

EntityGetBulkResponse.description: Partial-success envelope for `activity_get_bulk`. Top-level (no `message` wrapper). `summary` is `{requested, found, not_found}`; `results[]` is input-ordered, `results[i]` is the i-th requested id. A found row carries `data` (the entity); a missing/out-of-scope id reports `not_found` in place.

data.description: The entity (present on a found row).

MinimalUpsert.summary: Minimum viable: just enough to create a lead
MinimalUpsert.description: Only the dedup key (`mobile_no`) plus mandatory `first_name`/`status` (or let them default-fill). No routing, no profiles. Useful for an absolute-minimum smoke test.

UpsertWithOneProfile.summary: Add one profile child: lab values for an insurer lead
UpsertWithOneProfile.description: A Lab Profile row is attached. Typical of an insurer pushing a lab-screened lead.

InsurerLabIntakeLead.summary: Full: insurer-screening lead (labs + policy + alt phone)
InsurerLabIntakeLead.description: Realistic shape for an inbound insurer feed. Plan Profile for policy/payment, Lab Profile for the full panel.

OncologyPSPLead.summary: Full: oncology PSP lead (drug program + care team)
OncologyPSPLead.description: Illustrative shape for a Group A / Program B clinical lead. The Plan Profile fields shown are examples only; the actual fields for a key come from `lead_schema`. Care and Providers carries the assigned coach, doctor, and hospital.

WellnessSubscriptionLead.summary: Full: wellness subscription lead (plan + score + care team)
WellnessSubscriptionLead.description: Realistic shape for a Product Line C-style subscription sign-up. Plan Profile carries subscription + UTM; Lab Profile carries metabolic score; Care & Providers carries the assigned coach stack.

UpsertSuccessUpdated.summary: lead_create response: updated (existing lead found on the same line)

LeadSchemaResponse.summary: lead_schema: a key granted labs + plan fields

data.child_write: Send each child as a JSON array under its key. Multi-row children are upsert-by-key on key_field: a new key adds a row, the same key updates that row (only sent fields change), omitted rows are untouched. Single-row children merge onto the one row. Delete a row with {<key_field>, "_delete": true}.
data.dedup: A lead is unique per (mobile_no, product line, group). Re-sending the same phone updates that lead. Program is not part of identity: sending the same phone with a different program transitions the same lead, never a new one.

routing.note: Your routing is fixed. Any routing fields you send are ignored.

CuratedLeadGet.summary: lead_get: one curated lead with children

LeadUpdateRequest.summary: lead_update: flip status on a known lead

value.name: CRM-LEAD-2026-00123
value.summary: lead_update: flip status, upsert one lab row by its key

LeadListResponse.summary: lead_list: page of curated leads (no children)

ActivitySchemaResponse.summary: activity_schema: types available to a lead

ActivityCreateRequest.summary: activity_create: log a welcome call (deduped on external_id)

ActivityListResponse.summary: activity_list: page of a lead's activities

CallCreateRequestAttribute.summary: call_create: no lead, server strict-matches the customer number

RateLimit-Limit.description: The key's request budget for the current window. Sent on every partner response. A shared global ceiling is enforced separately, so a 429 can occur on the global limit even while RateLimit-Remaining is above zero. Absent when rate-limit enforcement is off or the caller is exempt.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests still available in the current window. Sent on every partner response. Absent when rate-limit enforcement is off or the caller is exempt.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the window refills and the budget resets. Sent on every partner response (success and 429). Absent when rate-limit enforcement is off or the caller is exempt (a System Manager with no mapping).

Retry-After.description: Sent only on a 429: seconds to wait before retrying. Mirrors `error.retry_after` in the body.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (`error.code` is `rate_limited`). Throttling is enforced against both the per-key budget and a shared global ceiling; the call is limited if either is exhausted. `Retry-After` or `error.retry_after` seconds are waited, then the call is retried (every write is idempotent, so retrying is safe).

get.description: Confirms the `Authorization` header is correct by returning the account the key belongs to. Suitable as the first call when integrating, and as a health check in CI: anything other than `200` means the auth is wrong. Setup: [Authentication](/partner-validate-key).

Returns the exact fields the key may send and read, which of them are required, the routing mode, and how each child table behaves. Called instead of hardcoding a field list, since two keys return different schemas. Full walkthrough: [Schema discovery](/discover-schema).

200.description: The caller's allowed fields + routing mode under `data` (no `message` wrapper).

403.description: The key is not permitted to make this call.

post.description:
Create-or-upsert a call log. `external_id` and `direction` are required. Idempotent on `external_id` (stored in `custom_external_id`): re-sending updates the same row and never doubles.

**Attribution is fail-closed; `lead` is read.** `lead` or `mobile_no` attaches explicitly (line-scoped); omitting both lets the server strict-match the customer number (`from_number` on Inbound, `to_number` on Outbound) within the caller's line. No match, or an ambiguous (2+) match, leaves the call unlinked and `lead` returns `null`, never on a wrong lead.

200.description: Call created or updated. **Read `data.lead`**, it is `null` when attribution found no/ambiguous match (the call is unlinked).

403.description: The key is not permitted to make this call.

404.description: An explicitly-sent lead or mobile_no was not found, or is outside the caller's line (identical, to prevent enumeration). Server-attribution misses do not 404; they return `lead: null`.

A row may succeed yet still be unlinked (`lead: null`), but the bulk result reports `name`/`external_id`, not `lead`; read each back via `call_get`/`call_list` to confirm linkage.
